mainTopic: When a non-Jew or an עם הארץ may have touched wine or pure items, and when we assume they did not
overview: This amud brings several real-life stories about wine that a non-Jew might have touched. רבא permits wine near a gentile girl holding froth, because she probably took it from the outside of the barrel. An army opened many barrels in נהרדעא. רב דימי reports that רבי אלעזר permitted such a case but is unsure why, and the גמרא defends one possible reason: the soldiers were hunting for money, not wine. A wine-shop owner gave her key to a gentile woman, and the בית מדרש ruled that she only handed over the job of guarding the key. אביי supports this from a משנה about keys and טהרות, which leads to a dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן about a courtyard split by a low partition. Each side is challenged from ברייתות about courtyards and roofs, and each is defended. The amud ends with a new משנה: soldiers who enter a city in peacetime make open barrels forbidden, but in wartime all barrels stay permitted.

steps.title: The gentile girl holding wine froth
steps.stepSummary: A gentile girl is found among wine barrels holding froth. רבא rules the wine is permitted, because she probably took the froth from the outside of the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile girl was found among wine barrels, holding wine froth in her hand. רבא said: The wine is permitted. We can say she took the froth from the outside of the barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story and gives רבא's ruling: the wine is still permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that she put her hand inside a barrel and touched the wine, which would make it forbidden. רבא says there is another reasonable way she got the froth: from the outside of the barrel, where froth collects. Since that explanation works, we do not forbid the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: a young girl (here, a gentile girl)
the place of the wine barrels
the outside or top of the barrel

phrases.english: There was a certain girl who was found
that she was among the wine barrels,
and she was holding froth in her hand.
Rava said: The wine is permitted,
say that she took it from the outside of the barrel.
phrases.notes: The froth that bubbles over and sits on the outside of the barrel, not the wine inside.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine near a gentile girl holding froth is permitted, since she may have taken the froth from the outside of the barrel.

steps.title: Even if no froth is left outside
steps.stepSummary: Even if there is no froth on the outside of the barrel now, we may say she happened to find some there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though there is no more froth on the outside now, we can say she just happened to find some there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers a question before anyone asks it: what if we check and no froth is left on the outside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that if the outside has no froth, she must have taken it from inside. רבא says the froth she found may have been the only bit there, and she took it. Because it is still possible, the wine stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: it just happened to come her way

phrases.english: And even though there is no more,
phrases.notes: He means no more froth is left on the outside of the barrel.

phrases.english: say that she just happened to come upon it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's leniency to a harder version of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defends the ruling against an unstated objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If no froth is left outside, it must have come from inside the barrel.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may have taken the last froth that was outside, so the wine is still permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא permits the wine as long as there is a reasonable innocent explanation, even if we cannot see any evidence for it now.

steps.title: The army that opened barrels in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: An army came to נהרדעא and opened many wine barrels. רב דימי reports that a similar case came before רבי אלעזר and he permitted the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain army came to נהרדעא and opened many barrels. When רב דימי came, he said: A case like this came before רבי אלעזר, and he permitted the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story and brings an earlier ruling from רבי אלעזר that permitted the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soldiers opening barrels raises the fear that non-Jews touched the wine. רב דימי, who came from ארץ ישראל, reports a lenient ruling in a similar case. The reason for the ruling is not given yet, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: A certain army that came up to Neharde'a
opened many barrels.
When Rav Dimi came, he said:
There was a case before Rabbi Elazar,
and he permitted it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר permitted wine in barrels that an army had opened.

steps.title: רב דימי is unsure of the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי does not know why רבי אלעזר permitted it. It may be because he follows רבי אליעזר's rule that uncertain entry stays pure, or because most people who travel with the army are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not know whether he permitted it because he holds like רבי אליעזר, who says that an uncertain entry is pure, or because he holds that most of the people who go along with an army are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives two possible reasons for רבי אלעזר's lenient ruling and says he does not know which one is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one compares the case to a טומאה rule: if we are not sure someone entered an impure place, he stays טהור, so here too we are lenient. Reason two is about who did the opening: most of the army's helpers were Jews, so their touch does not forbid wine. The two reasons work very differently, and the גמרא tests the first one next.

keyTerms.meaning: a doubt whether someone entered (an impure place)

phrases.english: But I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: whether it is because he holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: An uncertain entry is pure,
phrases.notes: This is a טומאה rule: if it's unclear whether a person entered an impure place, he stays pure.

phrases.english: or because he holds:

phrases.aramaic: רוּבָּא דְּאָזְלִי בַּהֲדֵי פּוּלְמוּסָא יִשְׂרָאֵל נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: most of those who go along with an army are Jews.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: the ruling came from רבי אלעזר, and one possible reason is that he follows the opinion of a different חכם, רבי אליעזר.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling reported in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason led רבי אלעזר to permit the wine: the rule of ספק ביאה, or that most of the army's people were Jews?

steps.title: This is uncertain touching, not uncertain entry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the first reason: the soldiers clearly came and opened the barrels, so the doubt is about touching, not about entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, is this really a case of uncertain entry? It is a case of uncertain touching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי אליעזר's rule fits this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's leniency is about not knowing whether someone came in at all. Here we know the soldiers came and opened the barrels, so the only question is whether they touched the wine. That is a ספק מגע, a different kind of doubt, and the comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: a doubt whether something was touched

phrases.english: If so,
is this a case of uncertain entry?
It is a case of uncertain touching!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first explanation offered in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי אלעזר permitted the wine based on רבי אליעזר's rule of ספק ביאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The soldiers definitely came and opened barrels, so the doubt is only about contact with the wine, and ספק ביאה does not apply.

steps.title: They were looking for money, not wine
steps.stepSummary: Since they opened so many barrels, they were probably searching for hidden money, so they likely did not handle the wine. That makes it similar to uncertain entry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they opened so many barrels, say they opened them looking for money, and so it is like a case of uncertain entry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and saves the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening many barrels suggests the soldiers were hunting for valuables hidden inside, not trying to drink. If they were not interested in the wine, it is doubtful they touched it at all. So the case is treated like ספק ביאה, and רבי אליעזר's leniency can apply.

keyTerms.meaning: with the intention of finding money

phrases.english: Since many were opened,
say that they opened them with the intention of finding money,
and so it is similar to an uncertain entry.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so it fits the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The soldiers opened the barrels, so this is a doubt about touching the wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: They opened the barrels to look for money and did not care about the wine, so the case is like ספק ביאה.
steps.whatToRemember: When non-Jews open barrels only to search for money, the case can be treated like ספק ביאה, and the wine may be permitted.

steps.title: Giving the key to a gentile woman
steps.stepSummary: A Jewish wine-shop owner handed her key to a gentile woman. The בית מדרש ruled that she only gave her the job of guarding the key, not permission to go in, so the wine is not suspect.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain wine-shop owner gave her key to a gentile woman. רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אלעזר: A case like this came to the בית מדרש, and they said: She only gave her the job of guarding the key.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third story and gives the ruling of the חכמים in the בית מדרש: the wine stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear is that holding the key let the gentile woman go in and touch the wine. The חכמים say that giving someone a key to hold is not giving permission to enter. Since she had no right to go in, we do not worry that she did.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who owns or runs a wine shop

phrases.english: A certain wine-shop owner
who handed the key (key) to a gentile woman,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the Hebrew word for key in round brackets here, and some leave it out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Elazar said:
There was a case in the study hall, and they said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָסְרָה לָהּ אֶלָּא שְׁמִירַת מַפְתֵּחַ בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: She gave her only the guarding of the key alone.

steps.whatToRemember: Handing a non-Jew a key only makes them a guard of the key. It does not give them permission to enter, so we do not assume they went in and touched the wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile who was given a key was only trusted to guard it, not to enter, so the wine is not suspect.

steps.title: אביי brings support from a משנה about keys
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves the key ruling from a משנה: someone who hands keys to an עם הארץ keeps his pure items pure, so wine surely stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We learned this in a משנה too. If someone hands his keys to an עם הארץ, his pure items stay pure, because he only gave him the job of guarding the key. Now, if pure items stay pure, do we even need to say it about יין נסך?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up the בית מדרש's ruling from step 7 with an older source, a משנה about טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same reason as step 7: handing over a key means 'guard it', not 'go inside'. אביי then argues with a קל וחומר: the laws of טהרות are stricter, so if they are lenient here, יין נסך should be lenient too.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in an earlier source)
A Jew who is not careful about the laws of purity
Food and items kept in a state of ritual purity
Now that this is so, is the other case even a question? (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We too have also learned this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in טהרות 7:1.

phrases.english: One who hands keys to an am ha'aretz,
his pure items are pure,
because he did not hand over to him
anything except guarding the key alone.
Now, if his pure items are pure,
is there any question about libation wine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the בית מדרש's ruling in step 7 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that handing over a key does not make the wine suspect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in טהרות: one who hands keys to an עם הארץ keeps his pure items pure, plus a קל וחומר from טהרות to יין נסך.

steps.title: Are purity laws really stricter than libation wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions אביי's assumption that טהרות are stricter than יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that pure items are stricter than יין נסך?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the hidden assumption behind אביי's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's argument only works if טהרות are stricter. The גמרא asks whether that is really true, and the next step answers it.

phrases.english: Is that to say that pure items
are stricter than libation wine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the premise of אביי's קל וחומר in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the laws of טהרות are in fact stricter than the laws of יין נסך.

steps.title: Yes: רב's ruling on a courtyard split by a low partition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and shows it from רב, who is stricter with טהרות than with יין נסך in a courtyard divided by a low partition. רבי יוחנן is lenient in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As it was stated: about a courtyard divided by a low partition, רב said: his pure items become impure, but with a gentile neighbor the wine does not become יין נסך. רבי יוחנן said: even his pure items stay pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9: yes, טהרות are stricter, and here is a ruling that shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same courtyard, רב worries that an עם הארץ neighbor will reach over and touch pure items, but does not worry that a gentile neighbor will touch the wine. That shows רב treats טהרות more strictly. רבי יוחנן is lenient even for טהרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms אביי's קל וחומר at least according to רב, and it sets up the challenge against רב in the next step.

phrases.english: Yes, as it was stated:
A courtyard that was divided with a low partition:
Rav said: his pure items are impure,
but with a gentile, it does not make the wine libation wine.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even his pure items are pure.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב rules that pure items behind a low partition become impure, but wine near a gentile does not become יין נסך, so טהרות are stricter.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the חבר's inner courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a חבר may leave produce and vessels in his inner courtyard even though an עם הארץ next door can reach them. That seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If the inner courtyard belongs to a חבר and the outer one to an עם הארץ, the חבר may spread out produce and put vessels there, even though the עם הארץ's hand can reach there. This is difficult for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's strict ruling about pure items using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the עם הארץ can reach the חבר's things, yet we do not worry that he touched them. That seems to clash with רב, who worried about pure items behind a low partition.

keyTerms.meaning: A person careful about purity and tithes

phrases.english: They challenged from a baraita:
If the inner courtyard belongs to a ḥaver
and the outer one to an am ha'aretz,
that ḥaver may spread out produce there
and put vessels there,
even though the hand
of the am ha'aretz can reach there.
This is difficult for Rav!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that pure items behind a low partition become impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows a חבר's items to stay pure even though an עם הארץ can reach them, which contradicts רב's worry.

steps.title: רב answers: there he would be caught as a thief
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the ברייתא is different, because the עם הארץ would be caught as a thief if he touched the חבר's things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would tell you: It is different there, because he would be caught as a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing why the ברייתא's case is different from his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the inner courtyard belongs only to the חבר, so an עם הארץ reaching in would be treated like a thief, and he is afraid to do it. In רב's case of a shared, divided courtyard, there is no such fear, so the worry about touching stays.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (defending a view)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי proves the key ruling with a קל וחומר from טהרות. רב is stricter with טהרות than with יין נסך, and the ברייתא of the inner courtyard does not disprove him, because there the עם הארץ would be caught as a thief.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
It is different there,
because he would be caught for it as a thief.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows we never worry that an עם הארץ will reach over, which would go against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the ברייתא the עם הארץ fears being treated as a thief, so he will not touch. That reason does not apply to רב's divided courtyard.

steps.title: A higher roof is safe only if the neighbor cannot reach it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a חבר whose roof is higher than an עם הארץ's roof may put produce and vessels there, but only if the עם הארץ cannot reach. This seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if a חבר's roof is above an עם הארץ's roof, the חבר may spread produce and put vessels there, as long as the עם הארץ cannot reach them. This is a problem for רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to argue with רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן was lenient even when the עם הארץ could reach the items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said pure items in a courtyard split by a low partition stay pure, even though the עם הארץ can reach them. Here, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the עם הארץ can reach the items, they are not safe. So reaching distance seems to matter, against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: spreads out (for example, produce laid out to dry)
this is a difficulty: the source seems to contradict someone

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר לְמַעְלָה מִגַּגּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: If the roof of a chaver is higher than the roof of an am ha'aretz,
that chaver may spread out produce there
and place vessels there,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא יָדוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ מַגַּעַת לְשָׁם.
phrases.english: provided that the hand of the am ha'aretz cannot reach there.
This is difficult for Rabbi Yochanan!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב in step 12, the גמרא now challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's leniency regarding טהרות in a courtyard with a low partition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes the items' safety depend on whether the עם הארץ can reach them. רבי יוחנן is lenient even when he can reach.

steps.title: On the roof, the neighbor has an easy excuse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the roof case is different. An עם הארץ caught reaching up can say he was only stretching, so he is not afraid to touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: it is different there, because he has a way to get out of it. He can say, 'I was just stretching myself.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the roof ruling does not contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's courtyard case, the עם הארץ would be caught red-handed if he touched things, so he holds back. On the higher roof, he can hide what he did by claiming he was only stretching, so there is nothing stopping him. That is why the roof case is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there: the cases are not alike
to slip out of it, to get away with an excuse

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
It is different there,
because he has a way to slip out of it,
for he can say:
"I was just stretching myself."
phrases.notes: He can claim his hand just landed up there while stretching, so nobody can call him a thief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13. It uses the same 'fear of being caught' idea that רב used in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The roof ruling seemed to show that being within reach always makes the items unsafe.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being within reach matters only when the עם הארץ has an easy excuse. Where he would be caught as a thief, he holds back.

steps.title: A roof right next door is fine even within reach
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא says that if the roofs are side by side, the חבר may put produce and vessels there even though the עם הארץ can reach. This seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a חבר's roof is beside an עם הארץ's roof, the חבר may spread produce and put vessels there, even though the עם הארץ can reach them. This is a problem for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא uses a different ruling in the ברייתא to challenge רב, who was strict about טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said pure items in a courtyard split by a low partition become impure because the עם הארץ can reach them. This ruling says that even when he can reach, the items are fine. That is the opposite of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: beside, next to (at the same height)

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר בְּצַד גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: If the roof of a chaver is beside the roof of an am ha'aretz,
that chaver may spread out produce there
and place vessels there,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּדוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ מַגַּעַת לְשָׁם.
phrases.english: even though the hand of the am ha'aretz can reach there.
This is difficult for Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר בְּצַד גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוחנן, the גמרא turns back to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's strictness regarding טהרות in a courtyard with a low partition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows items within the עם הארץ's reach. רב forbids exactly that.

steps.title: רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that he does not have to follow this ruling. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that being within reach makes the items unsafe, and רב rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: isn't there רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who stands with me? I am ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers by siding with the other opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not try to explain away the 'side by side' ruling. He admits it argues with him. He points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires that the עם הארץ cannot reach, and that is רב's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't there…? (pointing to a supporting opinion)
who stands like me, who agrees with me

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי יוחנן each survive a challenge. רבי יוחנן says reach matters only when the עם הארץ has an easy excuse. רב simply follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires that the items be out of reach.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אִיכָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Isn't there Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
who holds like me?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 13: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allowed the roof only if the עם הארץ could not reach.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: What I say follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes the roof discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following a different תנא (the other opinion in the same ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be a final ruling against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ruling is only one side of a dispute. רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Soldiers entering a city: open versus sealed barrels
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a military troop enters a city in peacetime, open wine barrels are forbidden and sealed ones are permitted. In wartime, all are permitted, because there is no time to pour wine for idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A troop of soldiers entered a city. In peacetime, open barrels are forbidden and sealed barrels are permitted. In wartime, both kinds are permitted, because there is no free time to pour libations.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case about יין נסך. Non-Jewish soldiers have passed through a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In peacetime, the soldiers had time to touch or pour from open barrels, so those are forbidden. Sealed barrels are not suspected. In wartime, the soldiers are too busy to pour wine for idol worship, so even the open barrels stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: a military troop or search party
to pour wine as an offering to idols

steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling depends on whether the non-Jews had the opportunity and the free time to make the wine forbidden. This same kind of reasoning ran through the earlier discussion of keys and courtyards.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A military troop that entered a city:
in peacetime,
open barrels are forbidden,
sealed ones are permitted;
in wartime,
both these and those are permitted,
because there is no free time to pour libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the roof discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In peacetime, open barrels are forbidden and sealed ones are permitted. In wartime, all barrels are permitted, because the soldiers have no time to pour libations.
